nodes.name: Covalent coupling with naphthalene on rGO
nodes.procedure: Co-TAPP/rGO underwent Schiff base reaction with polynuclear hydrocarbons (naphthalene derivatives) to form Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO, confirmed by N 1s imine bond signal at ≈398.3 eV.
nodes.source_text: covalent coupling with polynuclear hydrocarbons of naphthalene... N 1s signal for imine bonds (C = N) at ≈398.3 eV in Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO confirmed the successful Schiff base reaction (Figure S6)

nodes.source_text: coordination with metal ions at the nodes... the binding energy of C = N in Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO shifted to a higher position (≈398.8 eV), attributed to the N 1s signal of Ni-N bonds

nodes.description: Alkaline OER performance in 1.0 M KOH three-electrode system
nodes.source_text: The electrocatalytic performance of the molecular nanojunction catalysts for OER was tested by exploiting a three-electrode system in 1.0 M KOH electrolyte at room temperature. The linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves of Co-TAPP/rGO, CoTAPP-HNA/rGO, and Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO are displayed in Figure 3a. The consequences show that Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO achieves a significantly higher current density (220 mA cm^{-2}) at the same potential (1.7 V vs RHE)... Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO exhibits a lower Tafel slope (53.9 mV dec^{-1})... Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements reveal that Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO has the lowest charge transfer resistance... The C_dl values for Co-TAPP/rGO, CoTAPP-HNA/rGO and Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO were found to be 3.25, 6.35 and 7.31 mF cm^{-2}, respectively.

nodes.description: AEM electrolysis cell polarization curves at 25°C
nodes.source_text: The AEM electrolyzer was configured with Pt/C as the cathode and molecular nanojunction catalysts as the anode. Specifically, the Ni/CoTAPP-HNA/rGO based AEM electrolyzer required only 2.09 V to reach 500 mA cm^{-2} in 1.0 M KOH at 25°C, outperforming both Co-TAPP/rGO and Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO

nodes.description: AEM electrolysis cell stability at 200 mA cm^{-2}
nodes.source_text: Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO demonstrated stable performance in 1.0 M KOH for at least 70 h at 200 mA cm^{-2} without obvious performance degradation

assemble molecular nanojunctions into a dual electrode system for overall water splitting (Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO || Pt/C), with corresponding water splitting potentials of 1.81 V (25°C) and 1.65 V (80°C) at a current density of 200 mA cm^{-2}

nodes.characterization_summary: UV-vis spectroscopy showed a progressive red shift in the Soret band of Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO compared to Co-TAPP, indicating enhanced conjugation and strengthened interaction with substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: UV-vis spectroscopy showed a progressive red shift in the Soret band of Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO compared to Co-TAPP ... strengthened the interaction between the molecular catalyst and the substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: N 1s XPS shows C=N at ≈398.3 eV in Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO confirming Schiff base reaction; in Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO shifts to ≈398.8 eV indicating Ni-N coordination; Co 2p3/2 shifts from ≈781.4 eV to ≈780.2 eV indicating electron transfer from Ni to Co; Ni 2p peaks at ≈855.2 and ≈872.7 eV confirm Ni2+.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) further verified the successful synthesis ... confirming the successful coordination of Ni2+.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES analysis shows Co:Ni ratio of 1:3.52 in Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) analysis exposed a Co to Ni ratio of 1:3.52 in Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES absorption edge position close to NiO indicates Ni2+ valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The absorption edge position of Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO, which is close to that of NiO, indicates the presence of Ni species in a positive valence state of Ni2+.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows dominant Ni-N peak at 1.57 Å; curve fitting reveals NiN1O5 coordination with Ni-N 1.97 Å and Ni-O 2.06 Å; absence of Ni-Ni path confirms atomic dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier-transformed extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) analysis ... without undergoing metal ion exchange with the Co-porphyrin.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA uniformly loaded on rGO surface with no significant morphology difference from rGO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image shows that there is no significant difference in morphology between rGO ... uniformly loaded on the surface of rGO.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM shows composite thickness increased from 1.8 nm (rGO) to 3 nm indicating successful molecular nanojunction formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: AFM measurements showed that the composite of Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA and rGO increased the thickness ... indicated the successful formation of molecular nanojunctions.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping reveals uniform distribution of C, N, Ni and Co across Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: corresponding energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping revealed a uniform distribution of C, N, Ni and Co across the Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows well-dispersed bright spots corresponding to single metal atoms on rGO; intensity profiles confirm Ni-Co atom pairs with average distance 1.07 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the aberration-corrected high angle annular darkfield scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) of Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO showed numerous bright spots ... consistent with the simulated configuration.

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS shows work function Φ decreases from 4.79 eV (rGO) to 4.66 eV (Co-TAPP/rGO), 4.62 eV (Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO), and 4.26 eV (Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO) indicating enhanced electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The work function (Φ) of rGO, Co-TAPP/rGO, Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO, and Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO were calculated to be 4.79, 4.66, 4.62, and 4.26 eV, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV shows reversible Co²⁺/Co³⁺ redox waves in Co-TAPP/rGO, Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO, and Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO; Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO exhibits negative shift in redox potential indicating enhanced catalytic activity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The reversible redox waves were observed ... corresponding to the redox reactions of Co²⁺/Co³⁺ couples in Co-TAPP/rGO, Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO and Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows peak at ≈388 cm⁻¹ for *OH adsorption (Co-OH), peaks at 476 and 553 cm⁻¹ for Co-O vibrations; Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO shows delayed Co-OH peak and earlier Co-O peak compared to Co-TAPP/rGO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A peak ≈388 cm⁻¹ was observed in the in situ Raman spectra indicating *OH adsorption to form Co-OH. Additionally, peaks at 476 and 553 cm⁻¹ correspond to Co-O vibrations.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-SEIRAS shows peak at ≈1227 cm⁻¹ for O-O vibration of *OOH confirming AEM; weaker *OOH vibration and lower O₂(g) potential in Ni/Co-TAPP-HNA/rGO vs Co-TAPP/rGO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the peak at ≈1227 cm⁻¹ was observed in the in situ attenuated total reflection surface enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS), corresponding to the O-O vibration of *OOH ... accelerates the catalytic reaction kinetics.
